assertions.subject: Trauma
assertions.quote: Bruises can be characterized by the following:

assertions.subject: Trauma
assertions.quote: Human bites appear as 2- to 5-cm oval or circular marks

assertions.subject: Trauma
assertions.quote: Measurement of the inter-canine distance of the bite may help distinguish between an adult's bite (3 to 4.5 cm), a small adult's bite (2.5 to 3 cm), or a child's bite (2.5 cm, a child's deciduous teeth)

assertions.subject: Trauma
assertions.predicate: bruising on knees, shins, and bony prominences
assertions.quote: Bruising in nonabused children is most commonly found on the knees, shins, and bony prominences

assertions.subject: Trauma
assertions.predicate: bruising on backside, shoulders, and arms
assertions.quote: Commonly, in abuse, bruises are found on the backside of the child, beginning at the neck and continuing down to the knees, including the shoulders and the child's arms

assertions.subject: Trauma
assertions.quote: Bruising in nonambulatory children is uncommon and is concerning for nonaccidental trauma
